findings.problem: Step 2 explicitly checks root identity, position/bounds and eleven direct children, but neither it nor the final-selection step explicitly requires a fresh complete subtree comparison against the admitted exact 162 IDs plus 140 alias IDs. A new or reparented leaf inside an existing copied unit can leave those checks unchanged. One-root deletion also removes that leaf; the generic changed-target refusal is insufficiently defined to establish that this descendant change is detected.

14-cleanup-plan-v1.md:13 captures top-level originals/order; it does not capture every protected nested node. Top-level order alone cannot detect a protected leaf moved beneath an existing copied unit.
findings.required_revision: Make a fresh bounded exhaustive subtree admission mandatory before deletion, preserving exact IDs including all I-prefixed and semicolon paths. Compare the complete 162+140 set, explicit available type/parent relations and eleven direct-child order to the reviewed evidence; reject any new, missing, moved, ambiguous or unverifiable node, any protected source/shared definition physically in the target subtree, or a size/return bound preventing complete output. The old 162 nodes have no saved historical type/parent map: obtain and freeze a current full map without claiming historical ownership. Bind the final sole selected root to that admitted inventory after the last navigation/await and stop/re-admit if intervening changes cannot be excluded. Do not broaden deletion targets or normalize aliases.
findings.acceptance: A corrected frozen plan defines explicit descendant-drift/ownership refusal, preserves exact aliases, and still permits only one normal-editor removal of frame 38:3157 after separate founder deletion approval. No external diagnosis or execution is authorized by this receipt.
